Article Title: Canada, US make progress on trade deal as Mark Carney pursues new Asian markets
Article Text:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said negotiations with the United States are moving forward, following a lengthy conversation with President Donald Trump and senior officials, even as Ottawa works to expand trade ties across Asia and reduce its reliance on the American market.Speaking to reporters in Manila on Saturday, Carney said he had a “quite a long, substantive conversation” with Trump shortly before leaving for his trip to Europe and Asia.“We are making progress. There is the possibility of a deal, a bilateral deal. But we’re not yet there,” he said.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Trump's newly appointed White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, also took part in the discussion, Carney said.Ottawa, however, is not prepared to accept terms that could weaken its automotive industry, which has faced pressure from US tariffs.The latest discussions follow the breakdown of trade negotiations in August, when Canada suspended talks over last-minute demands from Washington that it considered unacceptable. The US subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, prompting Canada to introduce retaliatory duties in September.Negotiations have since resumed.A potential agreement could ease some of the tariffs affecting major industries, including steel and aluminium. However, the scope of any deal remains uncertain.Before the US midterm elections, Trump said the two countries were close to reaching an agreement. Carney later indicated that Washington had withdrawn demands concerning Canadian cultural policies, French-language protections and Ottawa's ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries.Trade tensions also became an issue during the midterm campaign. Democrats criticised the tariffs, linking them to higher consumer prices and promising to challenge the measures.Their electoral gains have complicated Canada's negotiating position. Ottawa must now weigh the possibility of securing partial tariff relief through an agreement against holding out for broader free-trade access as Congress prepares to scrutinise the existing measures.While discussions with Washington continue, Carney announced progress on two separate trade arrangements in Southeast Asia.Canada has substantially concluded negotiations on a free-trade agreement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a regional bloc representing nearly 700 million people. Ottawa has also completed negotiations on a separate agreement with the Philippines.The Canadian government estimates that the ASEAN deal could add nearly 2 billion Canadian dollars (US$1.4 billion) to the country's economy and support close to 14,000 jobs, particularly across agriculture and manufacturing. Officials expect to sign the agreement next year.The proposed Philippines agreement would cover more than 90% of tariff lines, Carney said. Ottawa expects the arrangement to help triple Canadian exports to the country by 2035, with formal signing also anticipated next year.Both agreements form part of Canada's wider strategy to diversify its export markets amid uncertainty over its trade relationship with the US.Carney has set a target of doubling Canadian exports to markets outside the US by 2035, making trade diversification a central part of his government's economic agenda.His visit to Manila comes ahead of a three-day ASEAN summit involving regional leaders and representatives from partner countries, beginning on Sunday.The prime minister previously attended the European Political Community summit in Ireland. His itinerary also includes the Francophonie summit in Cambodia and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, where he is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Article Summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has said negotiations with the United States are moving forward. Carney said he had a ‘quite a long, substantive conversation’ with President Donald Trump. The talks follow the breakdown of trade negotiations in August. The US subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.

Article Title: In 2006, a Baltimore developer promised to transform Poppleton into a new urban district; 20 years later, residents face a failed redevelopment and a Supreme Court refusal to hear their case
Article Text:
A sweeping vision that never materialised

A grocery store and wider redevelopment remain elusive

Why the residents took the fight to court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A two-decade redevelopment plan intended to reshape one of Baltimore's historic neighbourhoods has become the centre of a prolonged legal and community dispute, with little of the promised transformation materialising. Residents of Poppleton, a neighbourhood in West Baltimore, have now exhausted their latest legal option after the US Supreme Court declined to hear their challenge against the city and New York-based developer La Cité Development. The decision, reported by The Baltimore Banner and The Baltimore Sun on November 9, 2026, brings a two-year federal court battle to an end. The residents had challenged a redevelopment arrangement that relied on the city's eminent domain powers to acquire hundreds of properties, arguing that the project had caused lasting damage to the neighbourhood without delivering the promised public benefits. Much of the land cleared for the development remains vacant, while the developer has completed only a limited portion of the original proposal. For residents who stayed behind, the stalled project has meant living alongside empty plots and unfinished promises for years.The redevelopment agreement dates back to September 2006, when Baltimore City entered into a deal with La Cité to transform approximately 13.8 acres of Poppleton into a mixed residential and commercial district.The ambitious proposal included around 1,650 housing units, including apartments, condominiums and homes, alongside approximately 100,000 square feet of commercial space. The plan was expected to bring new businesses, retail outlets and a grocery store to the neighbourhood.To make the development possible, the city agreed to acquire properties within the designated area, using eminent domain where necessary. More than 500 homes were included in the redevelopment footprint, with many residents displaced as buildings were acquired and demolished.However, the project encountered repeated delays, financial difficulties and disagreements between the developer and the city. Baltimore attempted to terminate the agreement in 2012, but La Cité challenged the move in court and retained its development rights. The agreement was subsequently amended several times in an effort to revive the project.A major financial commitment followed in 2015, when the developer received approval for approximately $58 million in tax increment financing to support redevelopment and infrastructure work. Despite these measures, construction progressed slowly. The first major residential development, CenterWest, eventually opened in 2019 after delays caused by water damage. The apartment complex, comprising two buildings and approximately 262 rental units, remains the principal completed residential component of the larger redevelopment plan.The gap between the original vision and what exists today has become increasingly difficult for residents to ignore. The promised grocery store never opened, while large portions of the cleared land remain undeveloped. Earlier in 2026, Maryland lawmakers redirected a $500,000 state grant originally intended to support a grocery store in Poppleton to Open Works Baltimore, a nonprofit organisation planning to establish another makerspace location in West Baltimore.The development's prolonged stagnation has also raised concerns about the impact on residents who continue to own property in the surrounding neighbourhood. The absence of promised commercial facilities and the presence of large vacant areas have become central to complaints about the project's consequences. The University of Maryland, Baltimore County's Baltimore Traces project, which documents Poppleton's history and redevelopment, has also highlighted how decades of urban renewal, demolition and displacement have shaped the neighbourhood.In 2024, the Poppleton Now Community Association and six residents filed a federal lawsuit against La Cité, the city and other officials involved in the redevelopment. Their central argument was that the use of eminent domain to acquire neighbouring properties had served private development interests rather than a genuine public purpose. They also maintained that the stalled project had harmed the surrounding community, including by affecting property values and leaving residents exposed to the consequences of prolonged redevelopment.A federal district court dismissed their claims in June 2025. The residents subsequently appealed to the US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. In May 2026, the appeals court upheld the dismissal of the central claims, finding that the residents could not bring a constitutional takings claim over properties that belonged to their neighbours rather than themselves. It also ruled that their private nuisance claim did not establish a valid basis for relief under the arguments presented.The residents then petitioned the US Supreme Court to review the dispute. However, on November 9, the court declined to take up the case, leaving the lower courts' outcome in place. For Poppleton residents, the decision closes another chapter in a long-running struggle over redevelopment, displacement and accountability. While the legal battle has ended at the federal level, the larger question of what happens to the neighbourhood and its remaining vacant land remains unresolved.
Article Summary: Residents of Poppleton, a neighbourhood in West Baltimore, have now exhausted their latest legal option. The US Supreme Court declined to hear their challenge against the city and New York-based developer La Cité Development. The residents had challenged a redevelopment arrangement that relied on the city's eminent domain powers.

Article Title: Former Canadian premier Danny Williams donated 185 acres of family land to protect rare lichens; the gift expands a Newfoundland nature reserve to 1,198 acres
Article Text:
Image: Chris LeDrew

How Danny Williams' family land became important habitat for rare lichens in Newfoundland

Why Danny Williams donated 185 acres to expand the Salmonier River Nature Reserve

What makes the boreal felt lichen habitat on Danny Williams' land so unusual

Which other at-risk species could benefit from the expanded Newfoundland nature reserve

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Newfoundland and Labrador premier Danny Williams and his family have donated 75 hectares, or about 185 acres, of family land to the Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) to protect rare lichen habitat. The land, located north of St. Catharines in Newfoundland and Labrador, has been added to the Salmonier River Nature Reserve, bringing the protected area to 485 hectares, or roughly 1,198 acres. The donation followed an NCC survey that found boreal felt lichen on the Williams family property. The species is listed as being of special concern under Canada’s Species at Risk Act and grows in only a few areas around the world. The newly protected land also contains forests and wetlands supporting other species at risk.The conservation project began after the Nature Conservancy of Canada approached Williams in September 2023 about the possibility of rare lichens growing on his family’s land. NCC subsequently organised a targeted lichen survey, which confirmed the presence of boreal felt lichen, a tree-dwelling species that is listed as special concern in Newfoundland under Schedule 1 of the federal Species at Risk Act.The survey also found blue felt lichen and frosted glass-whiskers lichen nearby, both of which are also listed as special concern. The findings prompted discussions about permanently protecting the property and its unusual habitat.Williams and his family donated 75 hectares of their land to NCC, allowing it to become part of the existing Salmonier River Nature Reserve. The addition increased the reserve from its previous size to 485 hectares, or approximately 1,198 acres. NCC said the expanded reserve and its habitats will be conserved for generations. Williams described himself as a long-time advocate for environmental stewardship and said he was pleased to contribute after learning about the rare lichen and NCC’s plans to study and protect it. The donation also marks a decade of conservancy’s work in the Salmonier area.Boreal felt lichens are particularly dependent on mature and over-mature balsam fir trees, as well as decaying trees, and thrive in cool, moist conditions. NCC says the species is especially sensitive to the loss of mature forest because clearing can create drier conditions and remove potential host trees. The Salmonier River area provides those conditions through its forests, wetlands and distinctive climate. The reserve lies in the Avalon Forest Ecoregion, Newfoundland’s smallest ecoregion, where frequent fog collects over low-lying, sheltered bogs. The protected landscape therefore preserves more than the rare lichens themselves.The newly protected section of the Salmonier River Nature Reserve consists of forest and wetlands that provide habitat for several other species at risk. The conservancy identifies the red crossbill as threatened, while the olive-sided flycatcher is listed as special concern. The area also provides habitat for the little brown myotis and northern long-eared bat, both listed as endangered under Schedule 1 of the Species at Risk Act.The reserve also acts as a forested buffer for the 107,000-hectare Avalon Wilderness Reserve, which was established to protect barrens and forests supporting the Avalon woodland caribou herd, the most southerly caribou herd in Canada.
Article Summary: Former Newfoundland and Labrador premier Danny Williams and his family have donated 75 hectares, or about 185 acres, of family land to the Nature Conservancy of Canada. The land has been added to the Salmonier River Nature Reserve. The donation followed an NCC survey that found boreal felt lichen on the Williams family property. The species is listed as being of special concern under Canada’s Species at Risk Act.

Article Title: After losing his eldest son in a 2008 accident, Australian mechanic Gavin Hynam began restoring old cars for young people in need; he had donated at least 19 cars by 2025 and has now received a state
Article Text:
Gavin Hynam mentors young drivers, offering practical guidance, encouragement and support beyond driving lessons.

Personal tragedy sparks initiative that changes lives

More than just cars: Restoring old cars

Helping young drivers gain their independence

Generosity is a community effort

State recognition of an outstanding local hero

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

ABC News/Tamara Clark

For some, grief stays with them for a lifetime. But for Australian mechanic Gavin Hynam, the loss of his oldest son became the beginning of a mission that has changed the lives of young people all over regional Victoria. The 65-year-old has put his mechanical skills to work for his community, repairing discarded vehicles and handing over the keys to people who can’t afford transportation. Victoria’s 2027 Australian of the Year Local Hero, Bear, affectionately known as Hynam, has been recognized for his extraordinary generosity.Hynam’s dedication to community service started after his oldest son, Preston, died in an accident in 2008, just before he turned 21. And after years of grief, the Horsham-based mechanic has found a new lease of life helping young people tackle financial and practical barriers to independence.The idea began in 2017, when Hynam met two refugees who had recently resettled in the Wimmera region, ABC News reports. He was impressed by their resolve to build new lives and knew that dependable transportation could make a huge difference in their opportunities.He used his professional mechanical skills to fix two second-hand cars and gifted them to the young men once they got their driving licenses. He later broadened the initiative to assist other migrants and disadvantaged young people. This became the basis of his Cars 4 Youth program.According to The Weekly Advertiser, Cars 4 Youth enables Hynam to acquire affordable used cars, make any needed repairs and have them road tested before handing them over to the deserving recipients. The donated vehicles also come with six months registration, relieving the burden on the young beneficiaries.By August 2025, Hynam had handed over at least 19 sets of car keys, ABC News reported. The Weekly Advertizer also reported separately on his commitment to the scheme, reporting that at the time of its coverage, 13 vehicles had been gifted.And the effects go beyond transportation. Recipients have been provided with the opportunity to go to university, find jobs, support their families and access vital community services.Alongside fixing vehicles, Hynam has spent plenty of time mentoring learner drivers through Victoria’s Transport Accident Commission’s L2P program.The initiative matches eligible learner drivers who lack access to a vehicle or supervising driver with volunteer mentors. Participants are guided and practice supervised driving to help them complete the required 120 hours and work toward getting their licences, adds The Weekly Advertiser report.Hynam also volunteers with the Center for Participation’s P21 driving practice program, reports The Weekly Advertiser. His role extends beyond teaching young people to drive, providing them with motivation, practical advice and a caring relationship at a critical time in their lives.The initiative has also garnered support from those who want to see Hynam’s work continue. Preston’s family came together to organize fundraising efforts in his memory, raising almost $8,000. In December 2024, a Wimmera business group added another $10,000 to the program, the Weekly Advertizer reported. Hynam has also put about $20,000 of his own money into the scheme, according to ABC News.Hynam has been named Victoria’s 2027 Local Hero by the National Australia Day Council for his commitment to helping disadvantaged young people achieve mobility and independence. The Australian of the Year announcement said he would join winners from other states and territories at the national awards ceremony in Canberra on January 25, 2027. His award acknowledges more than cars given. It recognizes how the personal loss of one man spurred years of practical kindness, mentorship and civic engagement.Every restored car is one more young person with the freedom to pursue education, find a job and build a better future, according to Hynam. His work continues to make a difference in the lives of others in memory of Preston.Image Courtesy:
Article Summary: Gavin Hynam, 65, has been named Victoria’s 2027 Australian of the Year Local Hero. The mechanic has been helping disadvantaged young people achieve mobility and independence. His Cars 4 Youth initiative has helped at least 19 young people gain access to affordable used cars.

Article Title: JD Vance weighs skipping 2028 presidential race after Republican midterm losses: Report
Article Text:
File photo: US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a ceremony

Iran war emerges as key factor in Vance's 2028 calculations

Vance faces challenge of rebuilding MAGA coalition

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think JD Vance should run for the 2028 presidential election? Yes, he should run. No, he should not run. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

DeSantis, Cruz and Kemp emerge as potential contenders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trump has not committed to backing Vance

US Vice President JD Vance is seriously considering not contesting the 2028 presidential election following the Republican Party's sweeping defeats in the November 3 midterm polls, as he weighs the future of the MAGA movement, divisions within the party and the political fallout of the Iran war, according to a CNN report.Interviews with around a dozen people close to Vance, including allies and advisers, suggest that the vice president is uncertain about whether he should lead the Republican Party into the next presidential contest.While he has not made a final decision and a White House bid remains an option, his deliberations have reportedly centred on whether any Republican can win in the political climate created by President Donald Trump "I wouldn't be surprised by any decision he makes," one person close to Vance told CNN. "He's only 42. He's young enough that he can have a comeback should this environment make success impossible. It just may not be his time."Vance, who was earlier regarded as a leading contender for the Republican nomination in 2028, has not set a timeline for deciding whether to run. Some of his supporters remain confident that he will enter the race, while others say the political environment could influence his decision.His fourth child, born earlier this year, had already prompted speculation within the White House that he might put his presidential ambitions on hold. The midterm results and the divisions within the Republican coalition have added to the uncertainty.The ongoing war with Iran has emerged as a major concern for Vance and his allies, who believe the conflict could affect the Republican Party's prospects in the next presidential election.One Vance ally said that the question was not whether the vice president could lead the party, but whether any Republican could win if the conflict continued."The question isn't if JD can do it. It's: If the Iran war is still happening, can any Republican do it?" the ally said. "If they don't end the war in Iran, no Republican has a shot at 2028."Vance's position on the conflict came into focus the morning after the midterm elections, when he attributed the Republican defeats to the war in a lengthy post on X."The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," he wrote, arguing that any assessment of the party's losses should begin with the decision to enter the conflict.He also called for the administration to focus on ending the war, addressing affordability and domestic challenges, and reconsidering America's relationship with Israel.Vance had expressed reservations about military action against Iran to Trump before the strikes were launched. However, his public criticism after the midterms reportedly caught some administration officials off guard.Trump had been informed about the planned post before it was published but privately criticised Vance for not publicly defending the decision to launch military operations. Two people familiar with the discussions said the president was "pissed off" that his vice president had not stood by the decision.Trump later said Vance had been right about the role of the war in the Republican losses, but should also have defended the decision to launch it."He was right, other than one thing," Trump told reporters on Sunday. "He should have made one other statement: 'If you had it to do again, would you do it again?' The answer is yes."A White House official said that the administration had been aware of the post beforehand and that Trump had been briefed.On Thursday, Trump asked Vance to step away from Iran negotiations and focus instead on corruption, telling him to direct his "complete and total attention" to the issue.Beyond the Iran conflict, Vance's immediate priority is expected to be rebuilding support for the MAGA movement after Republicans suffered losses across several voter groups in the midterms.Voters who had helped Trump win in 2024, including men, young people, Latinos and white voters without college degrees, had shifted away from the Republican Party. White House officials and advisers to both Trump and Vance have acknowledged the difficulty of winning them back.Vance's allies believe he could seek to revive the anti-establishment message that helped him secure a Senate seat and later the vice presidency. However, his position within the administration could make it harder to present himself as an outsider.A Democratic-controlled Congress could also provide Vance with a new political target after he spent much of the past two years blaming former President Joe Biden for problems facing voters.Rich Baris, a pollster closely associated with the MAGA movement, said that many Trump supporters felt betrayed by the administration's failure to make life more affordable and its decision to enter another foreign war."MAGA is dead," Baris said, arguing that Vance would have to rebuild confidence among voters who had lost faith in the Republican Party.The divisions have also created space for potential challengers, including conservative commentator Tucker Carlson, who has hinted at a possible third-party presidential bid. Baris said Vance could play a role in preventing a further split within the party.Several Republicans have already begun positioning themselves for the 2028 presidential contest, including Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, Texas Senator Ted Cruz and Georgia Governor Brian Kemp.Vance's supporters, however, have played down the emerging competition, arguing that a divided Republican field helped Trump secure the party's nomination in both 2016 and 2024.Vance's allies have also expressed confidence that he would have access to financial backing if he decides to contest the election. They have pointed to his relationships with billionaire Elon Musk and former PayPal chief executive Peter Thiel, among other wealthy supporters.However, questions remain over the future involvement of major Republican fundraising groups after their midterm spending failed to deliver the expected results.Turning Point USA, which had endorsed Vance, also saw several of its preferred candidates lose in Arizona, while its efforts in New Hampshire and Nevada did not make significant progress.A group of donors aligned with Vance, known as the Rockbridge Network, met in Houston this week to discuss the political landscape following the midterm elections, according to a source familiar with the meeting.The uncertainty over Vance's presidential plans also comes amid questions about his relationship with Trump and whether the president would support his vice president in a Republican primary.Vance has said he expects Trump's backing if he decides to run. However, the president has not committed to endorsing him.Trump has reportedly told aides and allies he wants to wait before intervening in the Republican presidential contest and assess how potential candidates perform.Asked by 60 Minutes whether he would eventually endorse a candidate, Trump replied: "Probably — not necessarily."Vance was added to Trump's 2024 presidential ticket partly as a potential successor, but the midterm results have opened up the Republican field, according to Schilling."I do think the field has been blown open," he said, "and there isn't an heir apparent."Vance has yet to announce when he will decide whether to run in 2028.
Article Summary: US Vice President JD Vance is seriously considering not contesting the 2028 presidential election. He weighs the future of the MAGA movement, divisions within the party and the political fallout of the Iran war. He has not set a timeline for deciding whether to run.

Article Title: A Michigan dad who delivers frozen pizzas was mocked by a prankster, strangers donated $784,000 to help his family, and then he asked them to stop and give to other families and charities instead
Article Text:
A prank that sparked widespread outrage

A stranger steps in to help

Why Zerod decided to pause donations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Michigan father of four who became the centre of an extraordinary fundraising campaign after being targeted by social media pranksters has decided to stop accepting donations, despite strangers raising nearly $785,000 for his family. Walter Zerod, a frozen pizza delivery worker for Red Baron, thanked thousands of supporters and encouraged them to redirect their generosity towards other families and charitable organisations ahead of the holiday season. According to reports by The Detroit News, LADbible and Dexerto, Zerod made the announcement on November 5, exactly one week after the fundraiser began attracting widespread attention. The GoFundMe campaign, organised by Arizona resident Luke Oakenshield, had collected $784,273 from approximately 22,800 donors against an original target of $900,000. The decision came after the viral incident transformed what began as an uncomfortable confrontation at a grocery store into a major online fundraising effort.The incident involved Zerod stocking frozen pizzas at a Meijer grocery store in Michigan when a social media prankster approached him and asked for the time. As Zerod took out his phone, the individual played a sound resembling an Apple Pay transaction and pretended to have taken $10 from him.What followed was a confrontation that quickly gained traction online. Zerod became increasingly frustrated as the prankster continued provoking him, explaining that he was already having a difficult day, had four children to support and was struggling to keep up with his mortgage payments. He also indicated that he had already worked beyond his scheduled hours and was eager to return home to his family.The footage drew considerable criticism online, with viewers questioning the practice of targeting people at work for entertainment and social media engagement. The Instagram account associated with the pranksters, reportedly called ThreeOfAKind, was subsequently deleted. Red Baron's parent company, Schwan's, also confirmed that Zerod remained a valued employee and that it had checked on his wellbeing following the incident. The company publicly expressed support for him as the video circulated.Moved by the footage, Luke Oakenshield launched the GoFundMe campaign on October 27, hoping to provide Zerod and his family with financial breathing room. The response was considerably larger than anticipated. Within days, donations poured in from thousands of people, taking the campaign past the $700,000 mark before it eventually reached $784,273.Interestingly, Oakenshield was also dealing with serious personal difficulties. The veteran was reportedly homeless and living in his car when he organised the fundraiser for Zerod. His own circumstances subsequently attracted attention, prompting another fundraising campaign to help him with housing, transportation and financial stability. The two men have since developed a friendship, with Zerod acknowledging the support Oakenshield provided during an otherwise difficult period for his family.In his November 5 update, Zerod announced that he was pausing the campaign after a week of overwhelming support. He said the donations and messages had made a significant difference to his family and allowed him to spend additional time at home. He also asked people who still wished to contribute to consider supporting other fundraisers, local charities or churches helping families in need during the holiday season.The fundraiser's status was subsequently changed to donations paused, with the total standing at $784,273.Zerod also indicated that he wanted to step away from the sudden public attention and concentrate on his family. Protecting their privacy and safety was a priority as the story continued to attract widespread interest. His decision has brought an unusual conclusion to a viral incident that initially centred on the humiliation of a worker simply trying to do his job. Instead of continuing to pursue the original fundraising target, Zerod has chosen to redirect public attention towards people who may still need help.For a family that was struggling to make ends meet just days earlier, the donations have offered considerable relief. His final appeal, meanwhile, has encouraged thousands of strangers to extend the same kindness to others.
Article Summary: Walter Zerod, a frozen pizza delivery worker for Red Baron, thanked thousands of supporters and encouraged them to redirect their generosity towards other families. The GoFundMe campaign, organised by Arizona resident Luke Oakenshield, had collected $784,273 from approximately 22,800 donors against an original target of $900,000.

Article Title: Third affair? Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had relationship with second employee - report
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after reports came out on multiple affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, after his resignation on Thursday.The latest revelation follows reports of two other extramarital relationships involving Huang, including one with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy, and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care.Reuters said it was not identifying the second employee. Attempts to reach the woman were unsuccessful.Also read - After Nvidia chips, Super Micro servers? DOJ probes Alice Huang over alleged shipments to China Nvidia declined to comment on the latest development. Jensen Huang, Powell and a representative for Nvidia's board did not respond to requests for comment. Alice Huang could also not be reached.Huang had admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, although he did not refer to her by name.The controversy had initially appeared to have the backing of Nvidia's board, which expressed confidence in Huang in a November 8 statement and announced an independent investigation into the matter. The board had also said there was no reason to believe that Nvidia's national security or corporate secrets had been compromised.However, reports of another alleged relationship with Powell intensified the crisis, eventually leading to Huang's resignation on Thursday.The developments have also drawn attention in Washington, with US officials reportedly examining the national security implications of Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The controversy has raised questions about potential security risks involving the world's leading artificial intelligence chipmaker.
Article Summary: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters. The latest revelation follows reports of two other extramarital relationships involving Huang, including one with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy. Attempts to reach the woman were unsuccessful.

Article Title: US Senator Chris Van Hollen announces bid to replace Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader
Article Text:
Chuck Schumer (left) faces first leadership challenge in decades as Van Hollen enters race

Van Hollen gets support from Sanders, El-Sayed

Disagreement over Schumer's leadership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Senate Democrats consider a change in leadership after their recent electoral success? Yes, fresh leadership can bring new ideas. No, experienced leadership should continue. It depends on the party's future goals. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader, challenging incumbent Democratic leader Chuck Schumer after the party's victories in the US midterm elections.Van Hollen said on Thursday that he was running because “the American people called for change” and argued that Democrats needed new leadership to respond to the election result.“It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said in a statement. “This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”The leadership election will be held by secret ballot in early December. It is expected to be the first contested election for the position of Democratic leader in decades, with senators privately debating whether Schumer should continue in the role.Schumer has said he has enough support to retain the position. In a statement following Van Hollen’s announcement, he welcomed discussions about the future of the caucus and reiterated that he had the votes to remain its leader.“I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.”Schumer has been speaking to Democratic senators since the election and working on the party's agenda for 2027. During private caucus meetings this week, he outlined a broad plan for the first 100 days of the new majority.“I’m going to win it,” Schumer told the news agency Associated Press in an interview last week.Van Hollen has received endorsements from independent Senator Bernie Sanders , who caucuses with Democrats, and Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.Sanders said the election result reflected a demand for a Democratic Party that would challenge powerful special interests and the billionaire class while fighting for working families.“The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats,” Sanders said.El-Sayed had also backed Van Hollen's leadership bid, saying the party needed “bold leadership” after the election.“I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience,” El-Sayed wrote on X. “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.”Sanders and Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan had called for new leadership at a press conference on Tuesday, although neither had then endorsed a specific candidate, AP reported.Several Democratic senators have publicly backed Schumer, including incoming Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Senator Jon Husted in last week's election.Maine Senator Angus King, an independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election, also defended Schumer after Van Hollen's announcement.“Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” King said, adding that Schumer was “one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history”.The contest follows divisions within the Democratic caucus that became more visible in spring 2025, when Schumer faced criticism after siding with Republicans on a spending vote.Although he subsequently led Democrats through a government shutdown and helped the party's candidates during the midterm campaign, sections of the party's base have continued to call for generational change.Van Hollen, 67, is 75-year-old Schumer's challenger. He has presented himself as a new face for the party and has also said he is considering a presidential run.Speaking to MS NOW, Van Hollen said his decision to contest the leadership position was driven by what he described as a broader demand for change in Washington.“This is not about any one individual, but it is about answering the call of the American people. We saw a huge outburst of democracy on Election Day — red states, blue states, purple states — and it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption and his wars and his cruelty, it was also about a call for a larger change to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favor of the very wealthy against working people, led by a corrupt political system,” he said.Van Hollen also criticised Schumer's involvement in Democratic primaries, accusing him of supporting establishment candidates instead of focusing on defeating Republicans.“We shouldn't have a leader who is getting involved in picking sides in open Democratic primaries, and we should be focused on defeating Republicans. We have two senators right now in the Senate who wouldn't be there if the current majority leader had his way.He supported establishment candidates in the primaries,” he told MS NOW.Van Hollen has also called for action against President Donald Trump over allegations of corruption, supported efforts to impeach defence secretary Pete Hegseth and urged Congress to defund the war in Iran.The December ballot will determine who leads the Senate Democratic caucus as it prepares to take control of the chamber in the next Congress.
Article Summary: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader. It is expected to be the first contested election for the position of Democratic leader in decades, with senators privately debating whether Schumer should continue in the role. Schumer has said he has enough support to retain the position.

Clashes broke out between masked protesters and police in Barcelona on Wednesday as tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike in 14 years, called by the country's major trade unions over the housing affordability crisis and rising cost of living.Around 120,000 people joined demonstrations in Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona, where some protesters set fire to rubbish bins, smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Officers fired tear gas to disperse the crowds, while transport and other public services across the country faced significant disruption.The disturbances in Barcelona continued into the evening, with a heavy police presence in the city centre. Some clashes took place along Passeig de Gràcia, near the iconic Plaça de Catalunya. Local media reported that protesters fired fireworks at police and looted shops, including a Lego store. Some were also seen attempting to enter an Apple Store.The unions said around four million workers participated in the nationwide strike, which was backed by Spain's two largest labour organisations, the UGT and CCOO, as well as tenants' associations protesting against rising rents and evictions.UGT chief Pepe Álvarez described the strike as a success, citing "massive" participation, while CCOO leader Unai Sordo said turnout was "very significant". However, participation varied across the country, with stronger support in coastal regions where housing pressures have been particularly acute.The walkout was the first general strike in Spain since 2012, when workers protested against austerity measures during the eurozone debt crisis. It comes less than three weeks before parliamentary elections scheduled for November 29.Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is seeking to make housing affordability a central election issue and shift the political debate away from corruption cases involving his inner circle and a deadly train crash last month. His Socialist Party, however, continues to trail in opinion polls.Spain faces a housing deficit of around 750,000 homes, which is projected to exceed one million by 2028, according to the country's central bank.With home ownership becoming increasingly unaffordable, demand for rental accommodation has risen sharply, putting further pressure on the market. The average monthly rent of 1,176 euros ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7 per cent of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.

Article Title: 'I may be jailed, they may try to kill me': Sheikh Hasina's defiant message on returning to Bangladesh
Article Text:
Hasina opens up on fears, threats and Bangladesh return

Denies ordering killings during 2024 uprising

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rejects International Crimes Tribunal verdict

Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the threat of arrest, imprisonment or even death would not stop her from returning to Dhaka, asserting that she would rather die in her homeland than stay away from her people.In a rare audio interview with news agency IANS, Hasina said she was fully aware of the risks involved in returning to Bangladesh but maintained that fear had never stopped her from doing what she believed was right.“Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life. Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right,” the exiled leader stated.Expressing concern over the situation in Bangladesh, Hasina said the country was going through a difficult phase, alleging that Awami League leaders and workers were being persecuted while ordinary people were suffering and losing their homes and livelihoods.She said the hardships faced by the people had strengthened her determination to return and stand by them, irrespective of the consequences.“Today, my country is going through a terrible time. Our leaders and workers are being persecuted. Ordinary people are suffering, and families are losing their homes and livelihoods. How can I stay away while my people face such hardship? I have spent my entire political life with the people of Bangladesh. Whatever happens to me, I want to stand beside them. If I have to die, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina told IANS.Addressing allegations over deaths during the 2024 uprising in Bangladesh, the former prime minister categorically denied ordering the killing of innocent people.Hasina accused the former Muhammad Yunus-led interim government of stopping a judicial inquiry she had initiated into the deaths and subsequently granting legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as “political resistance”.“Let me make one thing very clear. I never ordered the killing of innocent people. I reject that accusation completely. Every death was tragic. As Prime Minister, I had a responsibility to protect the lives of our citizens, and I wanted to know exactly what had happened. That is why, on July 18, 2024, I established a Judicial Enquiry Commission headed by a High Court judge. On August 1, I expanded it to a three-member commission so that every incident could be examined properly. But what happened after Muhammad Yunus assumed power? He stopped that investigation,” the former PM said.She questioned the interim administration's decision to halt the inquiry while pursuing murder cases against her and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers.“His administration subsequently granted legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as political resistance. At the same time, murder cases were brought against me and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers. If they really wanted the truth, why did they stop the judicial investigation that I had already established? Why should there be different standards of justice depending on someone's political identity?” she questioned.Hasina also rejected the proceedings of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) and the verdict against her, alleging that she was not given a genuine opportunity to defend herself.“As for the tribunal, I reject both the proceedings and the verdict. I was denied what I consider a genuine opportunity to defend myself. I will examine whatever lawful options are available to challenge that verdict,” she told IANS.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina says she would rather die in her homeland than stay away from her people. Denies ordering killings during 2024 uprising in Bangladesh. Rejects International Crimes Tribunal verdict against her. Says she was not given a genuine opportunity to defend herself.

Article Title: Russian couple behind Empire State Building climb could face deportation after plea deal falls through
Article Text:
Angela Nikolau next to Ivan Kuznetsov, as they depart the criminal courthouse in New York City, US, November 12, 2026. REUTERS

Lawyer warns of consequences if couple is deported to Russia

Couple climbed 1,454 feet to unfurl banner and propose
