A 19-year-old Pakistani teenager was mauled to death by a tigress after it was let out of its cage for a TikTok video shoot.The victim, identified as Talha, was working at a private breeding facility in Kahna, Lahore district, when the animal attacked him. He was rushed to a private hospital but died while undergoing treatment on Wednesday, according to local reports.Police identified the arrested farm owner as Fayyaz and the TikToker as Noman. Investigators allege that the influencer had visited the property to film a video and asked for the animal to be released from its enclosure. The animal subsequently lost control and attacked the worker, police said.The incident also triggered an investigation into an alleged attempt to conceal the circumstances of the death. Police said efforts were made to portray the attack as an incident involving a dog rather than a big cat. The animal has since been handed over to wildlife authorities.Authorities are examining whether the farm had the necessary permits to keep the animal and whether adequate safety measures were in place at the facility. A case has been registered and investigations into possible negligence are under way.In a statement, Lahore Police said that the pursuit of social media content could not come at the cost of human life. It said all aspects of the alleged negligence and the attempt to conceal the attack would be investigated.There has been some confusion in initial media reports over whether the animal was a tiger or a lion. Lahore Police's statement described it as a tigress.
Article Summary: The victim, identified as Talha, was working at a private breeding facility in Kahna, Lahore district, when the animal attacked him. Investigators allege that the influencer had visited the property to film a video and asked for the animal to be released from its enclosure.

Article Title: Imran Khan-Asim Munir deal? Sisters' release from jail, hospital visit spark buzz in Pakistan
Article Text:
Release of Imran Khan's two sisters and his hospital visit fuel speculation of a possible political understanding with Pakistan's military establishment

PTI ready to make peace?

Nawaz Sharif , Benazir Bhutto precedent

Why a deal may not be straightforward

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is Pakistan witnessing the first signs of a possible thaw between jailed former prime minister Imran Khan and the country's powerful military establishment? The release of two of his sisters and his recent hospital visit for eye treatment have come amid speculation that a political settlement involving Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir has taken place.His sisters, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were released on Thursday from Lahore's Kot Lakhpat Jail after the Punjab government withdrew their extended detention orders. The two had spent 53 days in custody after being detained ahead of a Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) protest march. Their sister Aleema Khan remains behind bars.The release came a day after Imran Khan was taken from Adiala Jail to Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for an eye examination and treatment. Doctors administered an injection for an issue affecting his right eye, besides treating his blood pressure. He was discharged in the early hours of Thursday and returned to prison.The developments have coincided with renewed speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi, however, dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday, saying Khan and his family would receive whatever relief the courts granted them.The possibility of a rapprochement is not entirely new. In August, one of Imran Khan's closest aides, PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari, had told Reuters that the former prime minister would not confront the military if released."If Imran Khan was released tomorrow, hypothetically, he wouldn't do anything that would effectively damage the country," Bukhari had said, describing him as "magnanimous".He had also suggested that Munir could take the initiative to ease tensions, saying the army chief could extend a "healing hand" to the country."That doesn't mean you go loggerheads with the establishment, with the military leader," Bukhari said, adding that personal grievances could be set aside in the national interest.The remarks marked a notable shift in the PTI's public rhetoric after years of confrontation with the military establishment following Khan's ouster in a no-confidence vote in 2022.Bukhari, however, had mentioned that there were no talks between the PTI and the military. He also acknowledged that it was unclear whether Khan himself shared the willingness to reconcile being expressed by party leaders outside prison.The latest speculation has also been fuelled by opposition leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai's claim in October that Khan could be facing pressure to accept an arrangement similar to those involving former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto.Sharif left Pakistan in 2000 after being ousted and imprisoned following the military coup led by General Pervez Musharraf. Bhutto spent years abroad in self-imposed exile after her government was dismissed in 1996.Achakzai alleged that the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz and Pakistan Peoples Party were part of a political arrangement that could pave the way for a similar outcome in Khan's case. However, he did not establish that any such agreement had been reached.An exile arrangement could potentially offer a way out of the prolonged confrontation, but there is no confirmation that Khan has agreed to leave Pakistan or that negotiations with Munir are under way.Imran Khan's relationship with the military establishment deteriorated after disagreements over key appointments and foreign policy. He has accused the military leadership, including Munir, of orchestrating his removal. The military denies interfering in politics.Despite being in prison since August 2023, Khan remains the central figure in Pakistan's political confrontation. His party continues to demand his release, access to family members and lawyers, and relief in the cases against him.The PTI's position also raises a crucial question: can its leadership outside prison negotiate or signal a compromise without Khan's explicit approval? Bukhari's August remarks came with the caveat that the former prime minister's own thinking might be different.For now, the signals remain contradictory. Two members of Khan's family have been released, he has received medical treatment, and a senior PTI aide has previously spoken of reconciliation. But the government has denied any political bargain, and there is no evidence of direct negotiations with Munir.Whether the latest developments represent isolated legal and medical decisions or the beginning of a fresh political opening remains the question.
Article Summary: Imran Khan's two sisters were released from jail on Thursday after 53 days in custody. He was also taken to a hospital for an eye examination and treatment. The developments have fuelled speculation about a possible deal involving Khan and the military establishment. Pakistan interior minister dismissed reports of any behind-the-scenes arrangement on Thursday.

Article Title: 74 militants killed in Pakistan security operations along Afghan border in 10 days
Article Text:
43 militants killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raids, 31 in Balochistan operations: Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani security forces have killed 74 militants in a series of raids and operations in the country's northwest and southwest regions bordering Afghanistan over the past 10 days, the Associated Press cited military officials Friday.The raids were conducted in Mir Ali and Orakzai districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where troops killed 43 militants and recovered weapons, ammunition and explosive devices, the military said in a statement.Separately, security forces killed 31 militants in multiple operations in Balochistan province since November 3, the military said. The province has been witnessing a bloody insurgency led by the rebel Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).Kabul has denied accusations of providing support to militant groups operating against Pakistan.The Pakistani Taliban are a separate group from, but allied with, Afghanistan's Taliban, who returned to power in Kabul in 2021. Several TTP leaders and fighters are believed to be operating from sanctuaries across the Afghan border, a longstanding source of tension between Islamabad and Kabul.
Article Summary: Pakistani security forces have killed 74 militants in a series of raids and operations in the country's northwest and southwest regions bordering Afghanistan. The raids were conducted in Mir Ali and Orakzai districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Separately, security forces killed 31 militants in multiple operations in Balochistan province since November 3.

Article Title: BLA claims 18 killed in suicide vehicle attack on Pakistan Army camp in Balochistan
Article Text:
Baloch Liberation Army claims responsibility for a suicide vehicle attack on a Pakistani Army camp in Balochistan, claiming 18 personnel were killed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Multiple casualties were reported in a VBIED attack at Pak army’s main camp in Mastung, Balochistan Thursday. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel.According to BLA, its Fidayeen attack, the Majeed Brigade, carried out an operation in the Kanak area of Mastung, targeting a Pakistani military camp with a suicide vehicle-borne improvised explosive device followed by an assault by its armed fighters who entered the premises and targeted military personnel.The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.The area has been on the boil since Wednesday. According to pro-BLA accounts on Telegram, Pak security forces were carrying out “operation Radd-ul-Fitna”, aimed at destroying tunnels allegedly made by Baloch rebels, on Wednesday and Thursday in the area.They claimed to have destroyed seven tunnels and seized arms, ammunition and explosives. In Musakhel, unidentified set ablaze construction machinery and a separate explosion destroyed a bridge in Mastung.On Wednesday, 13 Pakistani police personnel including a Deputy Superintendent of Police were killed after fighters from the rebel group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) launched a major attack targeting mobile police units in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Article Summary: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) took responsibility for the attack, claiming to have eliminated 18 personnel. The attack unfolded while a meeting of senior Pak Army personnel including colonel rank officials was underway when the mini-truck laden with explosives rammed into the main gate of the camp.

Article Title: 'Some good news': Two sisters of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan released from jail; elder sister, wife remain behind bars
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former Prime Minister Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday after the Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said.However, his elder sister and wife remain behind bars."Finally, some good news. Two of former PM Imran Khan's sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have been released from Kot Lakhpat Jail following the withdrawal of their detention orders," PTI senior leader and former federal minister Moonis Elahi said in a statement."Hopefully, Aleema sahiba and Bushra Bibi, will also be released soon," he added, referring to the cricketer-turned-politician's elder sister and wife, respectively.Meanwhile, another senior PTI leader, Zulfi Bokhari, asserted that the release of Imran Khan's two sisters would not "erase the suffering" endured by his family."The release of two sisters does not end the injustice or erase the suffering inflicted on Imran Khan’s family. The demand is clear -- no selective relief, no intimidation, and no further persecution," Bokhari told party supporters.Imran Khan's sisters were detained in September under a public safety law to prevent them from mobilising support for a nationwide protest demanding his release.Bushra Bibi was arrested in January 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.The 74-year-old PTI founder has been in prison since 2023 and faces more than 100 cases, including corruption charges and allegations of inciting violence.On Wednesday, PTI lawyers met Imran Khan at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail to discuss his ongoing court cases, a day after the Islamabad high court directed authorities to facilitate the meeting.The lawyers spent four hours at the prison before leaving without speaking to the media.According to PTI lawyer Latif Khosa, who was part of the delegation, Imran Khan was experiencing problems with his blood pressure and eyesight.
Article Summary: Two sisters of Pakistan's incarcerated former PM Imran Khan were released from a Lahore jail on Thursday. The Punjab government revoked their detention orders, leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) party said. But his elder sister and wife remain behind bars.

Article Title: Pakistan announces schedule for Guru Nanak’s 557th birth anniversary celebrations despite Attari-Wagah closure
Article Text:
Pakistan has maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side (Photo: PTI).

AMRITSAR: Despite the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah international land border following Operation Sindoor, the Pakistan government has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev, expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib.Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side, although pilgrim movement through it continues to be suspended by India.According to Pak media reports, the programme was finalised at a meeting of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (PSGPC), chaired by its president and Punjab provincial minister for minority affairs and human rights, Ramesh Singh Arora, to review arrangements for the celebrations.As per the schedule, Indian Sikh pilgrims are expected to arrive in Pakistan through the Attari international border on November 22. The main ceremony will be held on November 24 at Gurdwara Janam Asthan, Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev. The pilgrims are scheduled to return on December 1.Reacting to Pakistan’s announcement, Sikh scholar Jagdeep Singh said the proposed pilgrimage programme assumes significance amid strained India-Pakistan ties and the continued closure of the Attari-Wagah border after Operation Sindoor.“Keeping the border open would serve the interests of both countries and, above all, make it easier for devotees to visit their historic religious shrines,” said Jagdeep.Interestingly, while Pakistan maintains that the Kartarpur corridor is operational on its side and has expressed readiness to facilitate Sikh devotees, India has suspended pilgrim movement through it since May 2025.In a statement, Arora said Pakistani diplomatic missions had been instructed to facilitate visa issuance for Sikh pilgrims. He also urged India to allow the Sikh sangat to visit its historic shrines.According to reports, the arrangements reviewed at the meeting include air-conditioned buses, accommodation, langar, medical facilities, mineral water and currency exchange services. A Rescue 1122 ambulance will accompany every convoy of 20 buses to meet medical emergencies.
Article Summary: Pakistan has announced a programme for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev. It is expecting between 2,300 and 2,700 Sikh pilgrims from India for the November 24 event at Nankana Sahib. Pakistan has also maintained that the Kartarpur Corridor remains open from its side.

Article Title: 'Two eight-year-olds or four four-year-olds': Pakistani cleric's child bride 'joke' sparks outrage
Article Text:
Mufti Tariq Masood (Source: Wikimedia Commons)

Education and women's autonomy

Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood, who commands a large following across social media platforms, has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage.In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.One of the remarks highlighted in the report came from a viral video in which Masood joked that if someone could not find a 16-year-old bride, he could provide “two eight-year-olds” or “four four-year-olds”. The comment drew criticism from people who said it trivialised child marriage and normalised the sexualisation of minors.The Daily Mirror said the backlash was dismissed by supporters as a misunderstanding, with the remark defended as a joke taken out of context.The newspaper also pointed to Masood's repeated opposition to statutory minimum marriage-age laws. According to the report, he has argued that Islamic jurisprudence does not prescribe a universal minimum age of 18 and that parents or guardians should retain discretion over when a girl marries.A recurring theme in his sermons, the newspaper said, is the emphasis on physical development and perceived maturity rather than chronological age when determining whether a girl is ready for marriage. The preacher had made remarks discussing the physical suitability of girls aged nine and ten in the context of marital relations. Pakistan as a country has been grappling with child sexual abuse, forced marriages and gender equality and positioning such leaders as popular figures raises extreme concerns.The Daily Mirror also highlighted Masood's remarks on women's education, saying that some of his statements appear to place a husband's authority above a young wife's decision to continue her studies.It further cited comments about women marrying late, including references to them becoming “aunties”, and discussions of the benefits husbands derive from marriage.Masood has also been criticised for presenting early marriage as a way to manage men's sexual desiresMasood's sermons have reportedly become difficult to access after copyright complaints and takedown requests. Critics have alleged that this limits public scrutiny of his statements, while his supporters maintain that some remarks are circulated without their original context.Masood has built a substantial following on YouTube, Facebook and other social media platforms through a preaching style that combines religious instruction with informal language and humour. His reach extends beyond traditional religious institutions, particularly among younger and urban audiences.
Article Summary: Pakistani Islamic preacher Mufti Tariq Masood has faced criticism over a series of sermons and remarks defending child marriage. In a report published by Daily Mirror Sri Lanka, the influential Deobandi cleric's comments have been reported in detail.

Article Title: Pakistan militant attack kills 10 policemen in KPK's Kohat, gunbattle still under way
Article Text:
No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. (FIle photo)

At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Wednesday, officials told news agency AP.The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire between the attackers and security forces, local police official Faisal Khan said.Khan confirmed that two senior police officers were among those killed. He added that the gunbattle was still underway, but did not share further details.No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. However, suspicion is likely to centre on the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, which has intensified its attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.Pakistan has witnessed a rise in militant violence over the past few years, with much of it attributed to the TTP. The group is separate from the Afghan Taliban but shares close ties with it. The Afghan Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021.Islamabad has repeatedly accused Afghanistan's Taliban-led government of providing shelter to TTP fighters operating against Pakistan. Kabul has denied the allegations.
Article Summary: At least 10 police personnel, including two senior officers, were killed in a militant attack in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack occurred in Kohat district, where militants targeted vehicles carrying police officers, leading to an exchange of gunfire. No militant organisation has claimed responsibility for the attack so far.

Article Title: Pakistan court frames charges against 8, including grandson of deputy PM Ishaq Dar, in gang rape case
Article Text:
Pakistan deput​y PM Ishaq Dar (File photo)​​

A Pakistani court on Wednesday framed charges against eight suspects, including the grandson of deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, in connection with the gang rape of two foreign women , an official said.All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty, the official added.“Lahore court judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal framed charges against the suspects, who pleaded not guilty. He directed the prosecution to present its witnesses on December 9 so that the formal trial proceedings could begin,” the official said.Earlier, police in Pakistan's Punjab province had cleared Raza Dar and his four accomplices of charges in the case, instead charging three other employees of Ishaq Dar's grandson of raping the women.The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela. They were allegedly kidnapped and raped by Raza Dar and his four friends after arriving in Lahore on a business trip in June. Medical examinations confirmed that the women had been raped. They returned to their respective countries after recording their statements.According to the police report, the women met Raza Dar in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested more than $500,000. However, the women allegedly failed to provide further returns or repay the amount.In June, Raza Dar invited the women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They initially stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to the hill station of Murree voluntarily.The women were later taken to a house in Lahore's Defence Housing Authority, where they were allegedly held captive and pressured to repay the money. They were forced to transfer $19,500, as per the police report.Armed men guarded the women and threatened them with a knife, a gun and a broken piece of mirror. They also threatened to kill them and sell their body parts if they failed to meet the demands.The women eventually managed to escape after the vehicle in which their alleged captors were taking them to Lahore airport met with an accident.
Article Summary: Pakistani court frames charges against eight suspects in gang rape of two foreign women. All eight accused, including Muhammad Raza Dar, Ishaq Dar's grandson, pleaded not guilty. The victims were identified as Stephanie Adnana Mau-Arun of the Netherlands and Astrid Robinson Baracho of Venezuela.

Article Title: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan taken to hospital for eye check-up, treatment; shifted back to Adiala Jail
Article Text:
Imran Khan's health sparks concern

Qureshi also hospitalised

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison, news agency Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing officials.Khan, who is lodged in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, was taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), where he also received treatment for blood pressure-related issues, one of the officials said."He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell," the person said.The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years after losing power in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging that they are politically motivated. The Shehbaz Sharif government has rejected his claims.All but one of Khan's convictions have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending.His lawyers have repeatedly raised concerns over his health in prison, claiming that his condition has deteriorated and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.Wednesday's hospital visit is the first known instance of Khan being taken for treatment and subsequently returned to jail since August, when an earlier hospital visit was cut short.Meanwhile, a Pakistani court has directed jail authorities to allow Khan's legal team to meet him and his wife, his party said.Khan's hospital visit comes a day after his close aide and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) deputy chairman, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, was taken to a hospital in Lahore after collapsing inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail.According to a prison official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old former foreign minister was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment and remains hospitalised.Khan, who led Pakistan to its maiden ODI World Cup title in 1992, has been behind bars for more than three years. Concerns over his health and prison conditions have repeatedly been raised by his family, party members and supporters, including former international cricket colleagues.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was taken to hospital for an eye check-up and treatment before being shifted back to prison. The 74-year-old cricketer-turned-politician has been in prison for more than three years. He has faced multiple corruption charges, which he denies, alleging they are politically motivated.

Article Text: More debt, less development? Pakistan spends just 10% of annual budget

Article Title: Imran Khan aide, ex-Pakistan foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi collapses in jail; hospitalised
Article Text:
(With PTI inputs)

Pakistan's former foreign minister and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf vice-chairman Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore, a prison official said on Tuesday.According to the official, Qureshi suffered a dizzy spell while walking inside his barrack at Kot Lakhpat Jail on Monday, injuring his knee and arm in the fall.The 70-year-old leader was subsequently shifted to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology for treatment, the official added.Qureshi has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots, when Tehreek-i-Insaf supporters went on a rampage following the arrest of party chairman and former Prime Minister Imran Khan.Qureshi's counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar, confirmed that the veteran politician was taken to hospital after fainting and suffering a fall.Umar added that the PTI leader would remain under observation for 24 hours, after which doctors would decide whether he should continue treatment at the hospital or be shifted back to jail.Meanwhile, Qureshi's daughter alleged that her father had been jailed on "trumped-up" charges and accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent."Three and a half years ago, a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped-up charges. He not only fought the cypher case with resolve and courage but refused to sacrifice his principles at the altar of self-interest," Mehr Bano said."My father has been acquitted multiple times but remains behind bars due to the government's malafide. Over 90 bail hearings have gone by, but the record has yet to be produced. A man whose innocence has been proven again and again is being held... It is high time the judge establishes his authority and grants him bail," she demanded.Bano also highlighted her father's more than four decades of public service in Pakistan."He has served twice as Pakistan's foreign minister, and as parliamentary leader and vice-chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, he has fulfilled important responsibilities and protected Pakistan's interests. He has fought for the supremacy of the Constitution and democracy. He deserves justice and freedom," she stated.
Article Summary: Pakistan's former foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi was admitted to a hospital after collapsing in his barrack at a jail in Lahore. The 70-year-old has been in jail since August 2023 in multiple cases linked to the May 9, 2023, riots. His daughter has accused the federal government of keeping him behind bars with "malafide" intent.

Article Title: Lashkar terrorist Hafiz Saeed's political outfit loses Pakistan's parliamentary bypoll
Article Text:
Terrorist Hafiz Saeed was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League.

A political party linked to Mumbai terror attack mastermind Hafiz Saeed has suffered a defeat in a parliamentary by-election in Pakistan, with the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) retaining the seat.The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk.According to results announced by the Election Commission on Monday, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes. However, he was defeated by PML-N's Rashid Bashir Virk, who polled over 43,000 votes.The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, the Pakistan Peoples Party and Jamaat-e-Islami did not contest the by-election.The polling saw a low voter turnout and was accompanied by allegations of electoral malpractice. Voters in one village boycotted the election entirely, while five PML-N women lawmakers were issued notices seeking explanations over alleged violations of the election code of conduct.Rejecting the outcome, the PMML accused the ruling PML-N of widespread rigging and refused to accept the results.The party had also contested Pakistan's 2024 general elections but failed to win a single seat.Hafiz Saeed, who founded the banned terrorist outfits Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jamaat-ud-Dawa, was previously associated with the Milli Muslim League. The PMML later emerged as another political platform linked to him and reportedly enjoys the backing of Pakistan's establishment.
Article Summary: The contest took place on Sunday in the NA-77 constituency of Gujranwala district in Punjab, around 80 km from Lahore. The by-election was necessitated by the death of sitting lawmaker Mehmood Bashir Virk. Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Muhammad Ibrahim Gujjar secured more than 30,000 votes.

Article Title: Pakistani TV anchor Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home; police probe husband's claim of accidental firing
Article Text:
Pakistani TV anchorperson Rabia Ahsan shot dead at home in Rawalpindi

First Lady condemns killing, calls for transparent probe

A Pakistani television anchorperson, Rabia Ahsan, was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday, with police taking her husband into custody and seizing the suspected weapon, Pakistani media outlet Samaa reported.The incident took place in the Gulshanabad area of the city, where Ahsan worked as an anchor and programme host for a local private TV channel.City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera confirmed that Ahsan's husband had been detained and that the suspected weapon had been seized. He said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding her death.According to the CPO, a male domestic worker at the house told police that Ahsan's husband had claimed the gunshot was fired accidentally.Sukhera visited the crime scene along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations, the SSP investigations and a team of forensic experts. Teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) were collecting evidence from the house.The body was being taken to a hospital for a postmortem examination. Sukhera said a case was being registered and the investigation would be conducted on merit.Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari expressed deep sadness over Ahsan's killing and strongly condemned the violence.She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.Bhutto-Zardari also expressed concern over what she described as a “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.She recalled the murder of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture.The First Lady noted that the outcome of the investigation into Javed's murder was still awaited.
Article Summary: Rabia Ahsan was shot dead at her home in Rawalpindi on Sunday. Police took her husband into custody and seized the suspected weapon. Pakistan's First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari condemned the killing.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina's return to Bangladesh: India wants Dhaka to fulfil two conditions, says report
Article Text:
India wants Bangladesh army to fly her back, but there's a catch

Why does India want Sheikh Hasina back in Bangladesh

What has Sheikh Hasina said about returning to Bangladesh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Sheikh Hasina be allowed to appeal her death sentence? Yes, she deserves a chance for justice No, the court's decision should stand 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Over two years after Sheikh Hasina fled to India, New Delhi is reportedly looking to send the former Bangladesh prime minister back to Dhaka, but has laid down two conditions for Tarique Rahman's government.According to a BBC Bangla report, India wants Bangladesh to send a military aircraft to bring Hasina back from New Delhi. However, the proposal comes with conditions, as Hasina has been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court over her government's crackdown on protesters during the July 2024 uprising.The first condition is that the Bangladesh army must take responsibility for bringing its longest-serving leader Hasina back, preferably using a military aircraft. This would mirror her arrival in India aboard a Bangladesh military aircraft after she fled the country on August 5, 2024.The second condition is that Bangladesh must guarantee Hasina an opportunity to appeal her death sentence and face a fresh trial over allegations linked to the July 2024 killings.The BBC Bangla report said Hasina's continued stay in India has increasingly become an uncomfortable issue for the government, affecting its bilateral ties with Bangladesh and attracting international criticism.India has faced criticism for sheltering a former leader convicted by a Bangladeshi court in connection with the deadly crackdown on protesters, the report said.More than two years after Hasina sought refuge in India following the mass uprising in July 2024, New Delhi is increasingly looking for a way to resolve the sensitive issue with its neighbouring country.India's preferred option would have been for Hasina to move to a third country. However, repeated efforts by New Delhi to explore this possibility with different countries failed for various reasons, according to the report.Hasina has maintained that she intends to return to Bangladesh, previously telling news agency Reuters in an interview that she planned to go back in December 2026.However, she has not announced a specific date.The former prime minister has also acknowledged the risks involved in returning, including the possibility of arrest, imprisonment or even an attempt on her life."Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life.Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right," the exiled leader said in an audio statement.In an interview with news agency IANS, Hasina also expressed concern over the situation in Bangladesh. She alleged that Awami League leaders and workers were being persecuted, while ordinary people were suffering, losing their homes and livelihoods.She described the country as going through a difficult phase, raising concerns over the treatment of political supporters and the broader situation under the new Dhaka government led by Tarique Rahman.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court over her government's crackdown on protesters during the July 2024 uprising. New Delhi is reportedly looking to send the former Bangladesh prime minister back to Dhaka, but has laid down two conditions for Tarique Rahman's government. Article Title: Ties strained, India-Bangladesh consular talks postponed
Article Text:
Ties strained, India-Bangladesh consular talks postponed

DHAKA: The fifth Bangladesh-India consular dialogue - scheduled to be held in Dhaka on Nov 17-18 - has been postponed, indicating that bilateral mechanisms between the two countries appear to have stalled, with little tangible progress on key areas of cooperation.The dialogue was supposed to discuss former PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition, cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes, repatriating citizens detained in either country, securing the release and repatriation of fishermen, and fostering mutual legal cooperation.On Nov 3, an inter-ministerial meeting was held at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka as part of preparation for the consular dialogue between the two countries.The fourth round of consular dialogue was held on May 29, 2024, in New Delhi.
Article Summary: The fifth Bangladesh-India consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka on Nov 17-18. The dialogue was supposed to discuss former PM Sheikh Hasina's extradition, cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes.
